To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) a parametric mismatch measurement technique has been developed that can characterize mismatch fluctuation levels of tens of ppm, and that (b) this technique can be used to characterize mismatch fluctuations for any type of matched pair of circuit elements, including BJTs, MOSFETs, resistors and capacitors.

1) a new mismatch measurement system is presented that is capable of measuring the mismatch of a large number of parameters of a large number (up to 100) of matched devices; 2) the system has a very small uncertainty, typically below 10 ppm; 3) the mismatch of the parameters is measured by using the system in a fully automatic way, without any user interaction.
A parametric mismatch characterization technique is proposed that can characterize parametric mismatch down to tens of parts per million.
